name: Determining When All Three Boolean Variables Are Equal
description: Construct a program that receives the value of three boolean variables from the user and determines whether all variables have the same value, either all three True or all three False.
code:
#Step 1: Read the user input for the value of the first boolean variable (variable a)
text = input("Enter 1 if the value of the first boolean variable (variable a) is True, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 2: Determine whether the value of the first boolean variable (variable a) is True 
if input_num == 1 :
    a = True
else:
    a = False
#Step 3: Read the user input for the value of the second boolean variable (variable b)
text = input("Enter 1 if the value of the second boolean variable (variable b) is True, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 4: Determine whether the value of the second boolean variable (variable b) is True 
if input_num == 1 :
    b = True
else:
    b = False
#Step 5: Read the user input for the value of the third boolean variable (variable c)
text = input("Enter 1 if the value of the third boolean variable (variable c) is True, otherwise enter 0:")
input_num = int(text)
#Step 6: Determine whether the value of the third boolean variable (variable c) is True 
if input_num == 1 :
    c = True
else:
    c = False
#Step 7: Write the boolean expression to determine whether all the three boolean variables have the same value
result = (a == b and b == c)
#Step 8: Print the result
if result == True :
    print("Yes! All the three boolean variables have the same value.")
else:
    print("No! Not all the variables have the same value.")

2.content: text = input("Enter 1 if the value of the first boolean variable (variable a) is True, otherwise enter 0:")
commentList: Purpose: This line displays a question to the user asking them to type 1 (for True) or 0 (for False) and saves whatever the user types as a string in the variable text. You will convert that string to a number on the next line.

Syntax and behavior: input(...) shows the message inside the quotes and returns the user's response as a string. The = operator stores that string in the variable named text, so after this line you can use text to inspect what the user entered.

Common errors and misconceptions: if the user types anything other than a plain '0' or '1' (for example 'yes', 'True', '1.0', or leaves it blank), the later int(text) conversion will raise a ValueError. Leading or trailing spaces can also cause unexpected results unless you handle them.

What you should check or do next: you should validate or normalize the input before converting it. For example, call text = text.strip() and check if text is '0' or '1', or use a try/except around int(text) to handle invalid input and ask the user again.

Best practices: make the prompt as clear as possible (you already say 1 for True and 0 otherwise), consider using a more descriptive variable name like input_text, and handle invalid entries so the program doesn't crash if the user types something unexpected.
Purpose: you convert the text you just read from the user into an integer and store that number in the variable input_num so the program can check whether it is 0 or 1.
Syntax and meaning: int(text) calls Python's built-in int() to turn the string text into an integer, and the = operator assigns that integer value to the name input_num.

Potential errors and misconceptions: if the user types something that is not an integer representation (for example 'yes', '1.0', or an empty string), int(text) will raise a ValueError and your program will crash; note that input() always returns a string, so you must convert it before numeric comparisons.

Best practices: you should validate or clean the input before converting (for example use text = text.strip() and check text in ('0','1')), or wrap the conversion in a try/except block to handle non-numeric input and reprompt the user until they enter a valid value.

Alternative suggestions: instead of storing the raw number in input_num you could convert directly to a boolean (for example after validation use a = (int(text) == 1) or a = bool(int(text)) with caution), and use clearer variable names like num_a to make your code easier to read.
